tags: why does my dog smell everything
script: Your dog stops every few feet to sniff a patch of grass, a pole, a spot on the sidewalk that looks completely unremarkable to you, and the walk ends up taking twice as long as planned. From your dog's side, that sniffing isn't a distraction from the walk, it basically is the walk. Dogs have somewhere around forty times more scent receptors than humans, and a huge portion of their brain is dedicated purely to processing smell, so a walk packed with new scents is genuinely one of the most mentally stimulating things you can offer them. Every sniff is picking up information, which animals passed through recently, whether they were stressed or relaxed, even roughly how long ago they were there, it's basically reading the neighborhood's social feed. This is also why a shorter walk with lots of sniffing time can tire a dog out more than a longer walk on a tight leash with no stopping allowed. So next time the walk feels slow because of all the sniffing, that's not your dog being difficult, that's your dog actually getting the enrichment the walk is supposed to provide.
